note: Seed candidates for the Sextant recall corpus. Deliberately OVER-GENERATED: `forge.mjs --check` decides which are admitted, because a candidate the existing suite already catches would measure 'can the agent run npm test' rather than review recall. Edits are exact text substitutions with a uniqueness assertion, not patch files, so they are reviewable and apply deterministically.

strata.M-mutation: Mutation-style operators over app/src. Boundary flips, inverted comparisons, dropped guard characters, off-by-one. These are the ROR/COR/statement-deletion families measured as most coupled to real faults (Just et al., FSE 2014: 73% of real faults couple to common operators).
strata.M-hand: Hand-authored, for the ~17% of real faults no mutation operator reaches — 'mostly algorithmic changes or code deletion' (same paper). Stale React effect deps, removed ARIA state, async id-correlation races.
strata.M-lint: A deliberately lint-detectable defect. An EXPLICIT EXCEPTION to the green-lint admission gate: it is scored against the LINTER, not the critics, to verify the A1 handoff actually catches what the critics were told to stop filing. If the linter misses it, A1 is not safe to adopt.
strata.R-real: Real historical defects from E1's 21 review rounds, re-introduced. NOTE the honest framing: E1 ratcheted every confirmed finding into a test, so re-introducing one makes its guard fail. A Stratum R seed therefore re-introduces the defect AND removes the specific guard, and records which. The label is 'a real defect with its guard removed', not 'a reverted fix'.

seeds.note: EXPLICIT EXCEPTION to the green-lint gate. Scored against knip, not the critics: it verifies the A1 handoff catches what the critics were told to stop filing.
